newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end session quietly firmer.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end session quietly firmer.

text.p: Australian shares finished a quiet session modestly firmer on Wednesday with stocks holding on to early gains after Wall Street hinted that its recent rally was not yet complete.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed 7.9 points higher at 2,323.7, not far from its intra-day high of 2,328.6.
Turnover was steady during the session with key buying interest in cyclical stocks like building materials, transport and media as well as for a handful of base metal miners.
"It was a mixed bag. There were a few standout stocks like Lend Lease and News Corp but without much news people were just buying on the back of the Dow," a dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage said.
The dealer said the level of turnover was encouraging and suggested that investors were reasonably confident that Wall Street could continue to run higher in the lead-up to Christmas.
"It would take some dire news to send the market into a spin. I think most traders are comfortable to hold stock, particularly after last week's rate cut," the dealer said.
Beverage group Coca-Cola Amatil continued to be singled out for selling attention a month after its profit downgrade and following a cooler than usual start to the Australian summer.
Coca-Cola Amatil shares closed 28 cents weaker at A$12.62. (US$9.97).
Dealers said market direction was likely to be strongly linked to the fortunes of Wall Street for at least the next month with little local news seen impacting day to day trade.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about four to three, while about 30 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
